65: section StalkStructureHom
66: 
67: variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
68: 
69: /-- **The structure homomorphism into a stalk.** For a scheme `X` over
70: `Spec k` with structure morphism `f` and a point `x : X`, the canonical ring
71: homomorphism `k ⟶ 𝒪_{X,x}`: identify `k` with the global sections of
72: `Spec k`, take the germ at `f x`, and apply the stalk map of `f`. -/
73: noncomputable def stalkStructureHom (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (x : X) :
74:     CommRingCat.of k ⟶ X.presheaf.stalk x :=
75:   (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫
76:     (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.germ ⊤ (f x) trivial ≫ f.stalkMap x
77: 
78: /-- The `k`-algebra structure on the stalk `𝒪_{X,x}` of a scheme over
79: `Spec k`, induced by `stalkStructureHom`. Not a global instance: for objects
80: of `Over (Spec k)` it is installed as the scoped instance
81: `overStalkAlgebra`. -/
82: @[reducible] noncomputable def stalkAlgebra (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (x : X) :
83:     Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
84:   (stalkStructureHom f x).hom.toAlgebra
85: 
86: /-- The canonical map `Spec 𝒪_{X,x} ⟶ X` followed by the structure morphism
87: is `Spec` of the structure homomorphism. -/
88: lemma fromSpecStalk_comp_eq (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (x : X) :
89:     X.fromSpecStalk x ≫ f = Spec.map (stalkStructureHom f x) := by
90:   unfold stalkStructureHom
91:   rw [← Scheme.SpecMap_stalkMap_fromSpecStalk, Spec.fromSpecStalk_eq, ← Spec.map_comp,
92:     Category.assoc]
93: 
94: /-- **Over-`Spec k` triangles are structure-homomorphism compatibilities.**
95: For a local ring `S`, a morphism `g : Spec S ⟶ X` and any `ψ : k ⟶ S`, the
96: triangle `g ≫ f = Spec ψ` commutes iff the ring homomorphism
97: `𝒪_{X, g(𝔪)} ⟶ S` induced by `g` intertwines the structure homomorphisms.
98: Proved at the `Spec.map` level using that `Spec` is faithful. -/
99: lemma comp_eq_spec_iff {S : CommRingCat.{u}} [IsLocalRing S]
100:     (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Spec S ⟶ X) (ψ : CommRingCat.of k ⟶ S) :
101:     g ≫ f = Spec.map ψ ↔
102:       stalkStructureHom f (g (closedPoint S)) ≫ Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo g = ψ := by
103:   constructor
104:   · intro h
105:     apply Spec.map_injective
106:     rw [Spec.map_comp, ← fromSpecStalk_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc,
107:       Scheme.Spec_stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecStalk, h]
108:   · intro h
109:     rw [← h, Spec.map_comp, ← fromSpecStalk_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc,
110:       Scheme.Spec_stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecStalk]
111: 
112: /-- Variant of `comp_eq_spec_iff` at a fixed point `x` with the stalk
113: transported along `g(𝔪) = x`, matching the stalk data produced by
114: `specToEquivOfLocalRingAt`. -/
115: lemma comp_eq_spec_iff_of_base_eq {S : CommRingCat.{u}} [IsLocalRing S]
116:     (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) {g : Spec S ⟶ X} {x : X}
117:     (hx : g.base (closedPoint S) = x) (ψ : CommRingCat.of k ⟶ S) :
118:     g ≫ f = Spec.map ψ ↔
119:       stalkStructureHom f x ≫
120:         (X.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq hx.symm)).hom ≫
121:           Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo g = ψ := by
122:   subst hx
123:   have hcongr : (X.presheaf.stalkCongr (Inseparable.of_eq
124:       (rfl : g.base (closedPoint S) = g.base (closedPoint S)).symm)).hom = 𝟙 _ := by
125:     simp [TopCat.Presheaf.stalkCongr]
126:   rw [hcongr, Category.id_comp]
127:   exact comp_eq_spec_iff f g ψ

commit 768b6cbd40ca1882510ae086f7b72bc45e916b40
Author: Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>
Date:   Mon Jul 27 20:28:54 2026 +0800

    P-cluster: [kappa(P):k] = 1 is now a THEOREM on AJC curve hypotheses, not a reformulation
    
    Both predecessor sessions left the residue-degree fact "reformulated, not discharged":
    GlobalGeneration.lean §7's hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed derives it from three
    stalk-level instance binders, and its own docstring records that AJC constructs none of
    them -- so it "trades one unproved fact for three unbuilt instances". This closes that.
    
    New module RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean (sorry-free, 9 declarations):
    
      residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve : residueDeg k P = 1
      hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve : HasRationalResidues k P
    
    for a prime divisor P of a curve C : Over (Spec k) with k algebraically closed, under
    [IsIntegral] [IsLocallyNoetherian] [IsRegularInCodimensionOne] [LocallyOfFiniteType]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] -- and LocallyOfFiniteType SYNTHESIZES from smoothness, so
    these are exactly the hypotheses AJC's own headline curve already carries.
    
    Why the third binder disappeared rather than got built. §7's route runs through
    IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral, which needs the residue field integral over
    k, hence a Module.Finite k kappa_P gate AJC lacks. Mathlib's residueFieldIsoBase instead
    gets integrality from isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace. So the trade is
    one open fact out for a LocallyOfFiniteType hypothesis in, and that one is free.
    
    The two binders that WERE built, and the lemma that mattered:
      stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ : stalkStructureHom C.hom x = constMap C >> germ_top
      algebraMap_stalk_functionField     : the stalk k-algebra of Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra
          and the function-field k-algebra of Adelic/GateInstances AGREE on constants
    The second is the load-bearing one: without it the stalk-level argument cannot be read in
    the order language the adelic lane speaks.
    
    Closedness of the point costs nothing: isClosed_primeDivisor derives it from
    coheight_le_one_of_curve (FiniteMapToP1.lean) plus PrimeDivisor's own coheight = 1, since
    the generic point is maximal in the specialisation order hence has coheight 0.
    
    RECORDED INSTANCE DIAMOND: with TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra imported, `open scoped
    AlgebraicGeometry` activates overStalkAlgebra C x : Algebra k O_{C,x}, and at
    x = genericPoint its target IS K(C), so it competes with Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra for
    Algebra k K(C) -- and the two are NOT defeq (rfl fails; machine-checked). This module
    therefore opens only AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme and builds the stalk algebra as an explicit
    letI. Activating the scoped instance would silently re-pin sectionSub/orderGeSub/residueDeg
    to a different k-action than the rest of the lane. Documented in the module docstring.
    
    Checks: lake build 8582 jobs exit 0 (only pre-existing WeilDivisor sorry warning);
    lake env lean on the module exit 0; all 9 declarations #print axioms =
    [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Per I-0412 that is NOT sufficient evidence, so
    instantiability was probed separately: residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve applies at
    AJC's headline hypotheses with LocallyOfFiniteType left to synthesis, and elaborates.

commit 66b07198483327e5c4a209175db6697b26663671
Author: Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>
Date:   Mon Jul 27 20:31:23 2026 +0800

    P-cluster: the principal-degree leaf now rests on the LEDGER ALONE, not on ledger + residues
    
    Chains the residue discharge into GlobalGeneration.lean §6's three consequences, each of
    which previously carried the approximation statement `hres` as a second open hypothesis:
    
      degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve       : deg_k D = deg D              (NO open input)
      degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve   : deg (div g) = 0        (ledger only)
      exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_isAlgClosed_curve : uniform generation at b+1
    
    The middle one is the point. degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues took the closed
    ledger AND rational residues; this takes the ledger alone. So the open leaf
    Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero is down from two open inputs to one, and the
    remaining one is the ledger the whole lane already needs.
    
    deg_k = deg is now UNCONDITIONAL on curve hypotheses -- no hypothesis at all beyond the
    curve. That converts every weighted statement in the adelic lane into a statement about the
    geometric Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree the rest of the project uses.
    
    STILL NOT DONE, stated precisely so this is not misread as closing the leaf: hledger is the
    closed chi-ledger and remains not a theorem. LedgerClosure.lean has it on the whole effective
    cone from the one-point bump; the negative part needs an input the lane does not have
    (chi is not additive in the divisor, and D is not linearly equivalent to D+). The WeilDivisor
    sorry is deliberately left in place -- substituting would make a hypothesis-free theorem
    depend silently on the ledger.
    
    Checks: lake build 8582 jobs exit 0; three new declarations #print axioms =
    [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; and instantiability probed rather than inferred from
    the axiom line -- both degK_eq_degree and degree_principal_eq_zero elaborate at AJC's
    headline curve hypotheses ([IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible] over algebraically closed k) with LocallyOfFiniteType and
    IsLocallyNoetherian left to synthesis.

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

    31	   `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`, proved by factoring both through `Γ(C,⊤)`:
    32	   `stalkStructureHom = constMap ≫ germ_⊤` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, from
    33	   mathlib's `Hom.germ_stalkMap`), after which mathlib's
    34	   `functionField_isScalarTower` matches the two composites.
    35	2. `IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(C)` — a corollary of (1) (`isScalarTower_stalk_functionField`).
    36	3. `Module.Finite k κ_P` — **not needed at all** on this route, which is the substantive
    37	   simplification.  §7's argument goes through `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`,
    38	   which needs the residue field to be *integral* over `k` and hence a finiteness input that
    39	   AJC does not have.  Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` proves
    40	   `κ(x) ≅ k` for a closed point of a scheme **locally of finite type** over an
    41	   algebraically closed field, obtaining integrality from
    42	   `isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace` instead.  `LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom`
    43	   is a hypothesis a smooth curve satisfies, unlike a bare residue-finiteness gate.
    44	
    45	So the exchange is: one open fact **out**, and in its place a `LocallyOfFiniteType`
    46	hypothesis plus the closedness of the point — both genuinely available.
    47	
    48	## The closedness input
    49	
    50	`residueFieldIsoBase` needs `IsClosed {P.point}`.  For a prime divisor this is *not* an
    51	extra assumption: `Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean` proves
    52	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one`, and a prime divisor has `coheight = 1` by
    53	definition while the generic point has coheight `0` on a curve.  `isClosed_primeDivisor`
    54	below packages this, taking the one-dimensionality of the curve as the hypothesis
    55	`hdim` that the sibling file also uses.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`,
    60	  `isScalarTower_stalk_functionField` — the compatibility layer (item 1–2 above).
    61	* `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom` — `k → 𝒪_P → κ(P)` is **bijective** at a
    62	  closed point, from mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.
    63	* `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `HasRationalResidues k P`, **discharged**:
    64	  every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.
    65	* `residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `[κ(P):k] = 1`, the campaign's residue fact.
    66	* `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — the **unweighted** principal-degree-zero
    67	  statement, from the ledger, with the residue input now discharged rather than assumed.
    68	
    69	## A note on an instance diamond (read before adding imports here)
    70	
    71	With `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean` imported, `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry`
    72	brings in `overStalkAlgebra C x : Algebra k 𝒪_{C,x}`.  At `x = genericPoint C.left` its
    73	target `𝒪_{C,generic}` *is* `K(C)` by definition, so it competes with
    74	`Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra` for `Algebra k K(C)` — and the two are **not**
    75	definitionally equal (machine-checked: `rfl` fails).  Everything below therefore opens
    76	only `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, and constructs the stalk algebra as an explicit `letI`
    77	rather than by activating the scoped instance.  Activating it would silently re-pin
    78	`sectionSub`/`orderGeSub`/`residueDeg` to a different `k`-action than the rest of the
    79	lane uses.
    80	-/
    81	
    82	set_option autoImplicit false
    83	
    84	universe u
    85	
    86	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
    87	open scoped WithZero AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    88	
    89	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    90	namespace Adelic
    91	
    92	/-! ## §1. The stalk `k`-algebra and its compatibility with `K(C)` -/
    93	
    94	section StalkAlgebra
    95	
    96	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    97	
    98	/-- **The structure homomorphism into a stalk factors through the global sections.**
    99	`k → 𝒪_{C,x}` is `constMap C : k → Γ(C,⊤)` followed by the germ at `x`.
   100	
   101	Both sides are the stalk map of `C.hom` precomposed with `ΓSpecIso.inv`; mathlib's
   102	`Hom.germ_stalkMap` is exactly the statement that the germ commutes past a stalk map.
   103	This is the lemma that ties `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`'s stalk algebra to
   104	`Adelic/GateInstances.lean`'s function-field algebra, which is built from `constMap`. -/
   105	theorem stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   106	    (x : C.left) :
   107	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x
   108	      = Scheme.constMap C ≫ C.left.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial := by
   109	  rw [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.constMap, Category.assoc]
   110	  congr 1
   111	  exact C.hom.germ_stalkMap ⊤ x trivial
   112	
   113	/-- **The two `k`-algebra structures agree.**  The image of a constant `c : k` in `K(C)`
   114	is the same whether one goes `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)` (through `stalkStructureHom`) or directly
   115	`k → K(C)` (through `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra`).
   116	
   117	This is what makes the stalk-level argument of §2 usable in the order language of the
   118	adelic lane, whose `algebraMap k K(X)` is the latter.  Proof: rewrite the stalk map as
   119	`constMap ≫ germ` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`), then both sides are
   120	`algebraMap Γ(C,⊤) K(C) ∘ constMap` — the first by mathlib's
   121	`functionField_isScalarTower`, the second by `Scheme.algebraMap_functionField_eq`. -/
   122	theorem algebraMap_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   123	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) (c : k) :
   124	    algebraMap (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField
   125	        ((stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c)
   126	      = algebraMap k C.left.functionField c := by
   127	  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : C.left.Opens) := Scheme.nonempty_top_opens C.left
   128	  letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :=
   129	    C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk (⟨x, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
   130	  haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
   131	      C.left.functionField :=
   132	    functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨x, trivial⟩
   133	  have h1 : (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c
   134	      = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
   135	        ((Scheme.constMap C).hom c) := by
   136	    rw [stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ C x]; rfl
   137	  rw [h1, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
   138	  rfl
   139	
   140	/-- **The tower `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)`** — binder (2) of `GlobalGeneration.lean` §7, now built.
   141	Immediate from `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`. -/
   142	theorem isScalarTower_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   143	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) :
   144	    letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
   145	    IsScalarTower k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField := by
   146	  letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
   147	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun c => ?_
   148	  exact (algebraMap_stalk_functionField C x c).symm
   149	
   150	end StalkAlgebra
   151	
   152	/-! ## §2. `κ(P) = k` at a closed point, over an algebraically closed base
   153	
   154	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` gives `κ(x) ≅ k` as a `CommRingCat`
   155	iso for a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
   156	`k`.  What is needed here is the *ring-map* form: that the composite
   157	`k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` — the map the order language sees — is bijective.  That follows once
   158	the composite is identified with the iso's inverse, which is `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`
   159	below: an identity of `Spec`-morphisms, checked through `Spec.map_injective`. -/
   160	
   161	section ResidueBijective
   162	
   163	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   164	
   165	/-- **A prime divisor of a curve is a closed point.**  On an irreducible scheme all of
   166	whose points have coheight `≤ 1` (the curve condition, supplied by
   167	`coheight_le_one_of_curve`), a point of coheight `1` is not the generic point — the
   168	generic point has coheight `0` — hence is closed by
   169	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one` (`Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean`).
   170	
   171	This is why the closedness input of `residueFieldIsoBase` costs nothing here: it is part
   172	of what `X.PrimeDivisor` already asserts. -/
   173	theorem isClosed_primeDivisor {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X]
   174	    (hdim : ∀ w : X, Order.coheight w ≤ 1) (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
   175	    IsClosed ({P.point} : Set X) := by
   176	  refine isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one hdim ?_
   177	  intro hgen
   178	  -- the generic point is maximal in the specialisation order, so has coheight `0`
   179	  have hmax : IsMax (genericPoint X) := fun y hy => genericPoint_specializes y
   180	  have h0 : Order.coheight P.point = 0 := by
   181	    rw [hgen]; exact Order.IsMax.coheight_eq_zero hmax
   182	  rw [P.coheight] at h0
   183	  exact absurd h0 (by simp)
   184	
   185	/-- **The composite `k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` is the inverse of mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.**
   186	
   187	Both are morphisms `k ⟶ κ(x)` in `CommRingCat`; `Spec` is faithful, so it suffices to
   188	check the induced `Spec` morphisms agree, and there both sides unfold to
   189	`X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ C.hom` — the left by `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` plus
   190	`fromSpecStalk_comp_eq` (`Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`), the right by mathlib's
   191	`SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv`. -/
   192	theorem residue_stalkStructureHom_eq [IsAlgClosed k]
   193	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   194	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
   195	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x ≫ C.left.residue x
   196	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv := by
   197	  apply Spec.map_injective
   198	  rw [SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv, Spec.map_comp, Scheme.fromSpecResidueField,
   199	    ← fromSpecStalk_comp_eq, Category.assoc]
   200	
   201	/-- **`k → κ(x)` is bijective at a closed point of a curve over an algebraically closed
   202	base.**  Immediate from `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`: an iso of `CommRingCat` has
   203	bijective underlying ring map.
   204	
   205	This is the statement that replaces `GlobalScheme`'s three-binder route: no
   206	`Module.Finite k κ_P` gate is consumed, because mathlib obtains integrality of `κ(x)` over
   207	`k` from `LocallyOfFiniteType` through the Jacobson-space finiteness criterion. -/
   208	theorem bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom [IsAlgClosed k]
   209	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   210	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
   211	    Function.Bijective
   212	      ((C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom) := by
   213	  have h : (C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom
   214	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv.hom := by
   215	    rw [← residue_stalkStructureHom_eq C x hx]; rfl
   216	  rw [h]
   217	  exact (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
   218	    (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv).mp inferInstance
   219	
   220	/-- **Every stalk element is a constant modulo the maximal ideal.**  The surjectivity half
   221	of `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom`, restated as the approximation statement on
   222	the stalk: for `a ∈ 𝒪_x` there is `c : k` with `a − c ∈ 𝔪_x`. -/
   223	theorem exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal [IsAlgClosed k]
   224	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   225	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left))
   226	    (a : C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :
   227	    ∃ c : k, a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c ∈
   228	      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := by
   229	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom C x hx).surjective
   230	    ((C.left.residue x).hom a)
   231	  rw [RingHom.comp_apply] at hc
   232	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   233	  rw [← IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff]
   234	  change (C.left.residue x).hom _ = 0
   235	  rw [map_sub, hc, sub_self]
   236	
   237	end ResidueBijective
   238	
   239	/-! ## §3. `HasRationalResidues`, discharged
   240	
   241	The stalk statement of §2 is now translated into the order language of the adelic lane.
   242	The translation has two steps and both are already available:
   243	
   244	* `f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0` lifts to `a ∈ 𝒪_P` — `exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg`
   245	  (`ChiLedger.lean` §N14b);
   246	* `a − c ∈ 𝔪_P` becomes `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1` — `mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal`
   247	  (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), whose statement is phrased on `orderGe P 1` rather than on
   248	  the raw inequality precisely so that `f = c` is admitted (the project's `ord_P 0 = 0`
   249	  convention would make the inequality form false there).
   250	
   251	The `k`-action bookkeeping is `algebraMap_stalk_functionField` (§1): the constant produced
   252	on the stalk and the constant the order language expects are the same element of `K(C)`. -/
   253	
   254	section Discharge
   255	
   256	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   257	
   258	/-- **`HasRationalResidues` holds at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
   259	closed field** — the residue fact of the campaign, now a theorem on AJC's own curve
   260	hypotheses rather than on unbuilt stalk binders.
   261	
   262	Compare `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), which proves the
   263	same conclusion but from `[Algebra k 𝒪_P]`, `[IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(X)]` and
   264	`[Module.Finite k κ_P]`, none of which AJC constructs.  Here the first two are built (§1)
   265	and the third is not needed (§2). -/
   266	theorem hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   267	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   268	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   269	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   270	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
   271	    HasRationalResidues k P := by
   272	  intro f hf
   273	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
   274	  · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
   275	    rw [map_zero, sub_zero]
   276	    exact (orderGe P 1).zero_mem
   277	  -- lift `f` to the stalk
   278	  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg hf0
   279	    ((mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf)
   280	  -- `P.point` is a closed point of the curve, so `κ(P) = k`
   281	  have hclosed : IsClosed ({P.point} : Set C.left) :=
   282	    isClosed_primeDivisor (coheight_le_one_of_curve C) P
   283	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal C P.point hclosed a
   284	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   285	  have himg := (mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal P
   286	    (a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom P.point).hom c)).mpr hc
   287	  rw [map_sub, ha, algebraMap_stalk_functionField C P.point c] at himg
   288	  exact himg
   289	
   290	/-- **The residue degree is one** at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
   291	closed base: `[κ(P) : k] = 1`.
   292	
   293	This is the fact that `SectionBounds.lean` §4 and `GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7 both reduce
   294	to and both leave open.  It closes item 1 of the two-item residue list in
   295	`SectionBounds.lean` §4. -/
   296	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   297	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   298	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   299	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   300	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor)
   301	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
   302	    residueDeg k P = 1 :=
   303	  (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr
   304	    (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   305	
   306	/-! ### The consequences, with the residue input no longer a hypothesis
   307	
   308	`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6 draws two conclusions from `HasRationalResidues` — uniform global
   309	generation with threshold `b + 1`, and the unweighted principal-degree-zero statement — but
   310	carries it as a hypothesis `hres`.  §3 above discharges `hres` on curve hypotheses, so both
   311	conclusions can be restated with **one** open input instead of two.
   312	
   313	Read the remaining hypothesis carefully: `hledger` is the closed χ-ledger, and it is *still*
   314	not a theorem in this project.  `Adelic/LedgerClosure.lean` proves it on the whole effective
   315	cone from the one-point bump (`chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg`) and states the remaining half
   316	exactly as an `iff` (`chi_eq_iff_step_of_bump`); the negative part needs an input the lane
   317	does not have.  So what follows is a genuine reduction from two open inputs to one, not a
   318	discharge of the leaf. -/
   319	
   320	/-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree on a curve over an algebraically closed
   321	base.**  `deg_k = deg`, with the residue-degree-one input discharged rather than assumed.
   322	
   323	This is what makes the adelic lane's weighted statements into statements about the geometric
   324	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` that the rest of the project uses. -/
   325	theorem degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   326	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   327	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   328	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   329	    [∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
   330	    (D : C.left.WeilDivisor) :
   331	    degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D :=
   332	  degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
   333	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   334	
   335	/-- **Principal divisors have geometric degree zero on a curve over an algebraically closed
   336	base, given the closed ledger** — the adelic route to the open leaf
   337	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, now resting on the **ledger alone**.
   338	
   339	Compare `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6),
   340	which takes both the ledger *and* the approximation statement.  The second hypothesis is
   341	gone here.
   342	
   343	This is the sharpest honest form of the leaf reachable today.  It is deliberately **not**
   344	substituted into `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, whose statement mentions no
   345	hypotheses: doing so would make a hypothesis-free theorem depend silently on the ledger. -/
   346	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   347	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   348	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   349	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   350	    [∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
   351	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
   352	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
   353	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
   354	    {g : C.left.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
   355	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
   356	  degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one k U₀ U₁ hledger hg
   357	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   358	
   359	/-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`**, with the residue input discharged.
   360	Above weighted degree `b`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global sections at *every* prime divisor,
   361	the residue-degree bound being `r = 1` on a curve over an algebraically closed base.
   362	
   363	Still single-field, and still conditional on the ledger, the base vanishing and the peel —
   364	see the three-gap discussion in `BoundedVanishing.lean`. -/
   365	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   366	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   367	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   368	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   369	    [∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
   370	    [∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
   371	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
   372	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
   373	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
   374	    (D₀ : C.left.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
   375	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : C.left.WeilDivisor,
   376	      (∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
   377	        (show C.left.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
   378	      Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D') :
   379	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
   380	      ∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P :=
   381	  exists_bound_forall_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel 1
   382	    (fun P => le_of_eq (residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P))
   383	
   384	end Discharge
   385	
   386	end Adelic
   387	end AlgebraicGeometry

461: /-! ## §5. What `[κ(P):k] = 1` actually says
462: 
463: Both the uniform generation statement (`r = 1`) and the open geometric leaf
464: `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` (through
465: `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, `SectionBounds.lean` §4) reduce to the
466: single fact `residueDeg k P = 1`.  It has been carried as an informal remark — "over an
467: algebraically closed base every closed point has residue field `k̄`".  This section
468: replaces the remark by a **machine-checked equivalence** to a concrete, checkable
469: statement about rational functions:
470: 
471: `residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ every function of order ≥ 0 at `P` agrees with a constant to
472: first order at `P`.`
473: 
474: That is `residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`.  It converts the remaining leaf from
475: a claim about residue fields — which in this substrate would require identifying
476: `localStepTgt k P 1` with `IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)`, an
477: identification this project does not have — into an approximation statement in the order
478: language the substrate already speaks.
479: 
480: Note what is **not** claimed *in this section*: `HasRationalResidues` is not proved here for
481: an algebraically closed base.  Doing so needs the multiplicative structure of `κ(P)` (a
482: finite-dimensional *field* extension of an algebraically closed `k` is trivial —
483: `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`), and `localStepTgt k P 1` is
484: constructed here as a quotient of `k`-submodules with no ring structure on it.  Finite
485: dimensionality alone does not give dimension one for a mere vector space, so the gap is
486: real and is exactly the missing ring-structure identification.
487: 
488: **It is proved elsewhere now**, for a curve: `Adelic.hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
489: (`Adelic/ResidueField.lean`).  Note how it escapes the obstruction just described — it never
490: identifies `localStepTgt k P 1` with the stalk residue field.  It proves the *approximation
491: statement* directly, by lifting to the stalk and using that `k → κ_P` is onto there, and then
492: feeds it back through this section's equivalence to reach `residueDeg k P = 1`.  So the `iff`
493: above is what makes the discharge possible: the ring-structure identification is still absent,
494: and is still not needed.
495: -/

499: variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
500:     [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
501:     [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]
502: 
503: /-- **Every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.**
504: `∀ f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0`, some `c ∈ k` has `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1`.
505: 
506: This is the concrete content of "`κ(P) = k`", phrased in the order language rather than
507: through the residue field: the residue of `f` at `P` is the constant `c`.  Over an
508: algebraically closed base field it is the standard fact that a closed point of a curve
509: has residue field the base field; here it is an explicit hypothesis, and
510: `residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` shows it is *exactly* equivalent to
511: `[κ(P):k] = 1`. -/
512: def HasRationalResidues (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : Prop :=
513:   ∀ f : X.functionField, f ∈ orderGe P 0 →
514:     ∃ c : k, f - algebraMap k X.functionField c ∈ orderGe P 1
515: 
516: /-- **`[κ(P):k] = 1` is equivalent to first-order approximation by constants.**
517: 
518: `→` The quotient `localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 / orderGe P 1` has dimension one and
519: its class of `1` is nonzero (`nontrivial_localStepTgt_one`), hence spans; so the class of
520: any `f` is `c • [1] = [c]`, i.e. `f − c ∈ orderGe P 1`.
521: 
522: `←` Conversely, approximation says every class is a `k`-multiple of `[1]`, so the
523: quotient is spanned by one vector and has dimension `≤ 1`; with `1 ≤ [κ(P):k]`
524: (`one_le_residueDeg`) it is exactly `1`.
525: 
526: The `→` direction needs no finiteness instance; `←` produces one, since a space spanned
527: by a single vector is finite-dimensional. -/

616: /-! ## §6. The rational-residue case: `r = 1` and the unweighted degree
617: 
618: Under `HasRationalResidues` at every prime divisor — the substrate's form of "the base
619: field is algebraically closed" — the two hypotheses that §4 and `SectionBounds.lean` §4
620: left open both become discharged simultaneously, because both were the same fact:
621: 
622: * the uniform generation bound gets `r = 1`, so the threshold is `b + 1`;
623: * `deg_k = deg` (`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`), so the weighted statements
624:   become statements about the geometric degree — in particular the principal-degree-zero
625:   leaf.
626: 
627: This is the precise pay-off of §5: one approximation hypothesis, two consequences.
628: -/
629: 
630: section RationalResidueConsequences
631: 
632: variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
633:     [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
634:     [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
635: 
636: /-- **Rational residues everywhere give residue degree one everywhere.** -/
637: theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues
638:     (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
639:     [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
640:     (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : residueDeg k P = 1 :=
641:   (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr (hres P)
642: 
643: /-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`.**  With rational residues at
644: every point, the residue-degree bound of `exists_bound_forall_generatedAt` is `r = 1`, so
645: one threshold works for every point and the shift over the vanishing bound is a single
646: unit.
647: 
648: This is the classical shape: above `deg D ≥ b + 1`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global
649: sections everywhere.  It remains single-field. -/
650: theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_hasRationalResidues
651:     (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
652:     (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
653:     (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
654:       (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
655:         (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
656:       Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D')
657:     (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
658:     [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)]
659:     [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
660:     ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
661:       ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, GeneratedAt k D P :=
662:   exists_bound_forall_generatedAt k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel 1
663:     (fun P => le_of_eq (residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P))
664: 
665: /-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree, under rational residues.**  Together
666: with `degK_principal_eq_zero` this is the unweighted principal-degree-zero statement; see
667: `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` (`SectionBounds.lean`), whose residue
668: hypothesis is now reduced to `HasRationalResidues`. -/
669: theorem degK_eq_degree_of_hasRationalResidues
670:     (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
671:     [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
672:     (D : X.WeilDivisor) : degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D :=
673:   degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
674:     (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P)
675: 
676: /-- **Principal divisors have geometric degree zero, from the ledger plus rational
677: residues.**  The adelic route to the open leaf
678: `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, with both of its inputs now named: the closed
679: ledger and the approximation statement `HasRationalResidues`.
680: 
681: Compare `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`: that took residue-degree-one on
682: the support as a hypothesis; here it is derived from the approximation form, which is the
683: statement one can actually hope to discharge from algebraic closedness. -/
684: theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues
685:     (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
686:     (hres : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, HasRationalResidues k P)
687:     [∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
688:     {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
689:     Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
690:   degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one k U₀ U₁ hledger hg
691:     (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_hasRationalResidues k hres P)
692: 
693: end RationalResidueConsequences

Author: Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>
Date:   Mon Jul 27 20:28:54 2026 +0800

    P-cluster: [kappa(P):k] = 1 is now a THEOREM on AJC curve hypotheses, not a reformulation
    
    Both predecessor sessions left the residue-degree fact "reformulated, not discharged":
    GlobalGeneration.lean §7's hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed derives it from three
    stalk-level instance binders, and its own docstring records that AJC constructs none of
    them -- so it "trades one unproved fact for three unbuilt instances". This closes that.
    
    New module RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean (sorry-free, 9 declarations):
    
      residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve : residueDeg k P = 1
      hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve : HasRationalResidues k P
    
    for a prime divisor P of a curve C : Over (Spec k) with k algebraically closed, under
    [IsIntegral] [IsLocallyNoetherian] [IsRegularInCodimensionOne] [LocallyOfFiniteType]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] -- and LocallyOfFiniteType SYNTHESIZES from smoothness, so
    these are exactly the hypotheses AJC's own headline curve already carries.
    
    Why the third binder disappeared rather than got built. §7's route runs through
    IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral, which needs the residue field integral over
    k, hence a Module.Finite k kappa_P gate AJC lacks. Mathlib's residueFieldIsoBase instead
    gets integrality from isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace. So the trade is
    one open fact out for a LocallyOfFiniteType hypothesis in, and that one is free.
    
    The two binders that WERE built, and the lemma that mattered:
      stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ : stalkStructureHom C.hom x = constMap C >> germ_top
      algebraMap_stalk_functionField     : the stalk k-algebra of Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra
          and the function-field k-algebra of Adelic/GateInstances AGREE on constants
    The second is the load-bearing one: without it the stalk-level argument cannot be read in
    the order language the adelic lane speaks.
    
    Closedness of the point costs nothing: isClosed_primeDivisor derives it from
    coheight_le_one_of_curve (FiniteMapToP1.lean) plus PrimeDivisor's own coheight = 1, since
    the generic point is maximal in the specialisation order hence has coheight 0.
    
    RECORDED INSTANCE DIAMOND: with TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra imported, `open scoped
    AlgebraicGeometry` activates overStalkAlgebra C x : Algebra k O_{C,x}, and at
    x = genericPoint its target IS K(C), so it competes with Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra for
    Algebra k K(C) -- and the two are NOT defeq (rfl fails; machine-checked). This module
    therefore opens only AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme and builds the stalk algebra as an explicit
    letI. Activating the scoped instance would silently re-pin sectionSub/orderGeSub/residueDeg
    to a different k-action than the rest of the lane. Documented in the module docstring.
    
    Checks: lake build 8582 jobs exit 0 (only pre-existing WeilDivisor sorry warning);
    lake env lean on the module exit 0; all 9 declarations #print axioms =
    [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Per I-0412 that is NOT sufficient evidence, so
    instantiability was probed separately: residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve applies at
    AJC's headline hypotheses with LocallyOfFiniteType left to synthesis, and elaborates.

Author: Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>

    P-cluster: the principal-degree leaf now rests on the LEDGER ALONE, not on ledger + residues
    
    Chains the residue discharge into GlobalGeneration.lean §6's three consequences, each of
    which previously carried the approximation statement `hres` as a second open hypothesis:
    
      degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve       : deg_k D = deg D              (NO open input)
      degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve   : deg (div g) = 0        (ledger only)
      exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_isAlgClosed_curve : uniform generation at b+1
    
    The middle one is the point. degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues took the closed
    ledger AND rational residues; this takes the ledger alone. So the open leaf
    Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero is down from two open inputs to one, and the
    remaining one is the ledger the whole lane already needs.
    
    deg_k = deg is now UNCONDITIONAL on curve hypotheses -- no hypothesis at all beyond the
    curve. That converts every weighted statement in the adelic lane into a statement about the
    geometric Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree the rest of the project uses.
    
    STILL NOT DONE, stated precisely so this is not misread as closing the leaf: hledger is the
    closed chi-ledger and remains not a theorem. LedgerClosure.lean has it on the whole effective
    cone from the one-point bump; the negative part needs an input the lane does not have
    (chi is not additive in the divisor, and D is not linearly equivalent to D+). The WeilDivisor
    sorry is deliberately left in place -- substituting would make a hypothesis-free theorem
    depend silently on the ledger.

    headline curve hypotheses ([IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible] over algebraically closed k) with LocallyOfFiniteType and
